rules:
HEX - 7x7 board.

BOARD
The board is a rhombus (diamond) of 7x7 = 49 hexagonal cells. Columns are letters a..g
from left to right, rows are numbers 1..7 from top to bottom; a cell is letter + number, e.g. c3.
Because the cells are hexagons, every row is shifted half a cell to the right of the row above, and
each cell touches up to 6 neighbours: for cell c3 they are b3 and d3 (same row), c2 and d2 (row
above), b4 and c4 (row below). In general cell (column L, row R) touches (L-1,R), (L+1,R),
(L,R-1), (L+1,R-1), (L-1,R+1), (L,R+1). Cells such as b2 and c3 do NOT touch.

PLAYERS AND GOAL
Player 0 plays X and must connect the TOP edge (row 1) to the BOTTOM edge (row 7) with an unbroken
chain of touching X stones. Player 1 plays O and must connect the LEFT edge (column a) to the RIGHT
edge (column g) with a chain of touching O stones. The first player to complete a chain wins.

TURN ORDER
Player 0 (X) moves first; then the players alternate. On your turn you place one stone of your
symbol on any empty cell. Stones never move and are never removed. Passing is not allowed.

ACTION FORMAT
    place <cell>
Examples:  "place c3"   "place a1"   "place g7"
Placing on an occupied cell, a cell outside the board or any other text is illegal (first time: a
warning and the same turn again; second time: you lose the game). The arena sends the complete list
of legal moves every turn.

WHAT YOU OBSERVE
The board drawn as a slanted grid, "." = empty, the move history and whose turn it is.
Example (7x7, X stones on b2 and b3, an O stone on c3):
     a b c d e f g        (X joins top<->bottom, O joins left<->right)
  1  . . . . . . .  1
   2  . X . . . . .  2
    3  . X O . . . .  3
     4  . . . . . . .  4
      5  . . . . . . .  5
       6  . . . . . . .  6
        7  . . . . . . .  7
           a b c d e f g

HOW THE GAME ENDS AND IS SCORED
The game ends as soon as one player completes a chain between their two edges: that player wins
(score 1, loser 0). A draw is impossible in Hex: when the board is full one player always has a
chain, so the game lasts at most 49 moves (the move cap).
